description: Restore a pg_dump archive from the operator's workspace into a registered foreign Postgres connection (it can be a different server from the one dumped). Archives only: custom, directory and tar, detected from the file and restored through pg_restore, which runs no client-side commands, with every restore option as a parameter (clean, if_exists, create, data_only, schema_only, no_owner, no_privileges, single_transaction, exit_on_error, jobs, schema, table, index, function, trigger, section, use_list, transaction_size, role and the rest). A plain-text SQL file is refused with external_pg.plain_sql_restore_refused, because replaying it needs psql, whose backslash meta-commands run programs on this host outside the database's grants; dump with format custom, or run plain SQL with run_script. With create, the archive's own database name is checked against the platform database first. input_path is an ABSOLUTE path under a saved location. Vendor GRANTs alone decide what is created, replaced or dropped. Returns a queued job.
embedding_description: Restore a pg_dump archive into an external Postgres database, the same server or a different one: custom, directory and tar archives through pg_restore with clean, create, data only, schema only, single transaction and selective objects. Use it to copy a database to another server or to recover one; plain SQL files run through run_script.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). The outcome arrives when the job completes: {input_path, format, tool, messages}, where format is custom, directory or tar, tool is pg_restore, and messages is its stderr with the host removed.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued. Once delivered, report the archive format and any messages pg_restore printed. A failed restore may have applied part of the archive unless single_transaction=true; exit_on_error=true stops at the first error.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Restore a workspace pg_dump archive into a registered foreign Postgres connection with pg_restore.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: external_pg.plain_sql_restore_refused: input_path is a plain-text SQL file, not a pg_dump archive; only custom, directory and tar archives are restored. external_pg.client_tool_failed: pg_restore exited non-zero; the message carries its stderr with the host removed, for example 'errors ignored on restore: N' or the first error with exit_on_error. external_pg.client_tool_missing: pg_restore was not found. external_pg.invalid_params: input_path does not exist, format differs from the detected format, a wrongly typed option, or create on an archive whose database name could not be read. external_pg.platform_db_refused: the connection, or with create the archive's own database name, is the platform's own database. external_pg.export_path_refused: the path must be absolute, have the required suffix where specified, and lie under a saved path address, the session folder or solet home, outside the installation tree. Input files must already exist. external_pg.permission_denied: the role lacks a privilege the restore needs. external_pg.auth_failed / external_pg.api_error: authentication or connection failed.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: external_pg.plain_sql_restore_refused: dump again with format custom (or directory/tar) and restore that, or run the plain SQL with run_script. external_pg.client_tool_failed: read the named errors; rerun with clean and if_exists to replace existing objects, no_owner/no_privileges when the target lacks the dump's roles, or single_transaction to make the restore all-or-nothing. external_pg.permission_denied: ask the operator for the GRANT or restore with no_owner.
